root_cause: applyNdkSigner cleared the tracked local key but remembered nothing, so every later getNdk/connectNdk(privateKeyHex) (DM send/edit/delete, reactions, history, watchers) put a private-key signer for the stored local key back on the NDK singleton, signing publishes with the local key instead of the connected NIP-07/NIP-46 signer.
fix: ndkClient remembers the applied external signer: applySigner skips while it is set, the singleton is created with it, and only releaseNdkExternalSigner (called first in disconnectBunker/disconnectNip07) returns NDK to a local key. _activateNip46Signer/_activateNip07Signer do all throwing work before applying, so a failed activation leaves nothing bound.

tests_added.kinds: real singleton + real signers: sticky across connectNdk/getNdk(localKey) with signed-event pubkey; early apply before creation; release with/without key; local-mode rebind; getNdk() without key keeps signer; default relays; SSR null

mutation.survivors: equivalent: `if (externalSigner)` on singleton creation mutated to true assigns null instead of leaving undefined before any key is bound

retrospective.harder_than_needed: The sticky signer removed an accidental self-heal (the next connectNdk rebound to the local key), so every exit from external mode and every failed activation had to be audited; the reviewer found two such paths.
retrospective.surprised_by: In NIP-46 mode the stored local identity is deleted on activation and a fresh random key is generated on the next mount, so the old rebind could sign DMs under an entirely unrelated identity.
